$comment: The Bundu floor's hit-region rules, as cases both evaluators must answer identically: contracts/runner.ts (hitViolations) and mzizi-rs/contract-eval (hit_violations). The floor has two pointer tiers (owner ruling 2026-11-12, #660): 28px on a desktop (a fine pointer with hover), 49px on touch (a coarse pointer). `fine` and `coarse` are the drawn heights in px (null: the runner could not read one); `violations` is how many sentences each returns. Pinned by __tests__/density.test.ts and mzizi-ui's tests/contracts_json.rs.

cases.name: a button drawn at 36px keeps its hit region through the pseudo-element
a button drawn under 28px is too small to draw
a link drawn at 36px is its box: enough on a desktop
a link drawn at 36px on touch has only its box, under 49px
a native field drawn at 49px is fine
a native field drawn at 48px fails on touch only
a native field drawn at 36px on a desktop is fine (28px floor)
a native field drawn at 24px on a desktop is under the 28px floor
a button with its own after: utility keeps only its box, which fails on touch
a button that clips its overflow keeps only its box, which fails on touch
a menu row takes min-height, so a short row is covered
a menu row with its own min-h-* is only its box, which fails on touch
a listbox option is a composite row too
a calendar day is a grid cell, left as drawn
a row the runner cannot read is skipped
